title: Physics: correct collisions and grounded character
description: Set up proper Rapier3D physics so the character has correct collisions and stays grounded. Should look and feel AAA-quality — take inspiration from Bruno Simon's portfolio (https://bruno-simon.com) for how physics-based interaction feels polished and playful. Key requirements: character must be solidly on the ground (no floating/clipping), collisions with world geometry must feel tight and responsive, if the player runs off the edge of the map they should fall (no invisible walls at boundaries).

title: Migrate codebase to TypeScript
description: Migrate the portfolio codebase from plain ES modules (JS) to TypeScript. Covers sources/Game/, data/, and tests. Motivation: type safety across the Game singleton/Ticker event bus, Rapier physics bindings, and the data layer contracts currently validated only by unit tests. Needs a plan/spec before implementation (Vite + bun + Playwright toolchain updates, incremental vs big-bang strategy).
notes: PLAN (Gate 1, awaiting human approval): Big-bang migration on one implement/ branch — 2.2k LOC is too small for an allowJs transition period. Phases: (1) tooling: typescript, @types/three, typescript-eslint, tsconfig (strict, noEmit, moduleResolution bundler, vite/client types), ambient d.ts for rapier_wasm3d_bg deep import, add 'tsc --noEmit' typecheck to verify gate, widen lint/format globs; (2) data/ → .ts with exported interfaces (terrain first, then rooms, content-map); (3) leaf modules: Palette/ToonMaterials (keyof PALETTE), Events+Ticker (typed event map — core motivation), UI, Inputs; (4) core: Game singleton (drop constructor-return hijack, null-union late-init fields), Physics (Physics|null everywhere), Player/Camera/World, declare global Window.__game, fix Player.js:148 Vector3 literal. Keep .js import specifiers (TS resolves .js→.ts natively; zero import churn, CLAUDE.md convention intact). E2e specs + playwright config untouched (no app imports). Unit tests stay .js (bun resolves .js→.ts).
close_reason: TypeScript migration complete — all gates green

title: Deploy portfolio to Vercel via GitHub integration
description:
Figure out and set up deployment of the portfolio to Vercel through the GitHub integration (repo: github.com/AtunBetun/portfolio).

What needs to happen:
1. Connect the GitHub repo to a new Vercel project (vercel.com -> Add New Project -> import AtunBetun/portfolio). This gives auto-deploys: production on push to main, preview deployments per PR/branch.
2. Configure build settings in Vercel (or commit a vercel.json). Project specifics:
   - Framework preset: Vite
   - Build command: bun run build (vite build) — Vercel detects bun.lock and uses Bun for installs
   - Output directory: dist (vite.config.js sets root: sources/ with outDir: ../dist, so output lands at repo-root dist/)
   - Install command: bun install (auto-detected from bun.lock)
3. Verify WASM works in production: the app uses @dimforge/rapier3d via vite-plugin-wasm + top-level-await; confirm the built bundle loads on Vercel (correct .wasm content-type is handled by Vercel automatically).
4. base: './' in vite.config.js is fine for Vercel root deploys; no change expected but verify asset paths on the deployed URL.
5. Decide whether to add a vercel.json to pin settings in-repo vs relying on dashboard config.

Open questions:
- Does a Vercel account/team already exist for this? Needs the human to log in and authorize the GitHub app.
- Custom domain?
notes: No vercel.json or .vercel dir exists yet. Repo remote: https://github.com/AtunBetun/portfolio.git. Package manager: bun. Verify script: bun run verify (lint, format, unit, build, e2e).

title: Death mechanic and respawn system
description: When the player falls off the map (or dies in any other future way), implement a death/respawn mechanic. Needs to feel polished — not just a hard teleport back. Consider: fade to black, a short animation, respawn at last safe position or a fixed spawn point. Should be extensible for future death triggers beyond falling.

title: Auto-planning cron — schedule Claude to plan spitballed ideas
description: Set up a cron job (or scheduled task) that auto-runs Claude planning sessions on a schedule. The workflow: human spitballs ideas as beads issues, then Claude picks them up on a timer and writes plans/specs. Sessions should be interactive so the human can jump in whenever they want. Each session should be created with the bead name/ID so it's easy to find and resume. Goal: low-friction ideation pipeline where you just dump thoughts and structured plans appear.

Envision the mechanics — paddling, current, obstacles, finish line. This is the gameplay layer on top of the canal hub.
